sentences.text: This claim petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed by the petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- for the death of Srinivas M B in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 31.03.2021 at about 9.00 pm.,
when Srinivas M B (hereinafter referred to as deceased)
was riding a bike bearing reg.No.KA-02-ET-5458 from Bengaluru side towards Madavara side on Bengaluru -  SCCH-26 3 MVC 2461/2021 Tumkuru NH 48 road.

When he reached near Parle G sky walk, a TATA ACE vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-53-B- 7856 driven by its driver came from behind i.e.,
Bengaluru towards Tumkuru side in a high speed, rash and negligent manner, in a zigzag manner and hit to the deceased's vehicle.
As a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Prakriya hospital, Bengaluru, while under treatment succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
The body was shifted to Nelamangala government hospital and PM was conducted, then dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.1 lakh towards hiring vehicles, to perform last rite ceremony and obsequies.

3. On the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and aged 40 years, working as Finishing Manager at Mittal Clothing company Unit -1,
No.471/D2, 4th phase, Peenya industrial area,
Bengaluru and was getting a monthly salary of  SCCH-26 4 MVC 2461/2021 Rs.40,000/- per month.

Whenever the  contract is entered, it creates right and  obligation between them.

Hence these documents go to shows that the policy issued by the respondent No.1 to pertain the two wheeler and not the policy issued to the TATA ACE Vehicle.

Further by perusing the FIR marked as per Ex.R.8 in Mumbai City, Dadar Police Station in Crime No.735/2022 it goes to shows that the respondent No.1 Company has lodged the complaint with regard to the fake policies issued by the some other persons in the name of their company.
Hence they goes to shows that with regard to the issuance of  SCCH-26 23 MVC 2461/2021 fake policy the respondent No.1 has taken appropriate steps by lodging the police complaint.

Hence by perusing the entire oral and documentary evidence adduced by the respondent No.1 goes to shows that the Policy No.3005/A/33999519/00/B00 is fake policy and the same is not issued to the TATA ACE Vehicle.
Further to disbelieve the evidence of RW.1 nothing worth is brought on record in the cross examination of RW.1.
Further the respondent No.2 who has appeared through his counsel has not at all contested this petition.
25. As per Sec.134(c) of the M.V.Act, the owner has to furnish the necessary particulars of the policy and vehicle in favour of insurance company, but he has failed to furnish the same.

Further as per Sec.147(a) of the M.V.Act policy shall be issued by the authorized insurer, but in the case on hand, copy of the policy furnished by the R1 is not issued by the authorized agent, but in the case on hand, R2 has failed to comply the above cited provisions of law.

Hence it goes to shows that the policy was fake policy and the same was not issued to the TATA ACE Vehicle bearing registration No. KA-33 B- 7856
